task.description: Validate src/design/iss0622-quota-usage-table-schema-qualification.md (fix design for GH-576/ISS-0622). Independently verify: (1) schemaNameForTenant's implementation (src/db/pool.zig:137-155) really has no SQL-metacharacter risk given the design's injection-safety claim in section 3.3 -- read the function yourself, don't trust the design doc's transcription; (2) resolveAndCacheStorageMode and applyRequestStorageRouting (pool.zig:183-301) really behave as section 4 describes for .LEGACY_RLS mode -- confirm tenant_default is genuinely the only applicable schema name, no other candidate exists; (3) the current structure of src/api/middleware/quota_enforcement.zig's readUsageForDimension/countRows/countRowsWhereRecent/maxColumn/sumColumn/tableStorageBytes matches what the design describes (line numbers, branch structure) -- read the file in full; (4) the design's decision to resolve schema once in readUsageForDimension rather than per-helper is followable as an implementation instruction (i.e. concrete enough for BACKEND-DEV to implement without re-deriving design decisions); (5) confirm the repository_artifacts branches are correctly identified as untouched/already-correct; (6) confirm the tableStorageBytes finding (a 5th call site with the same bug, not in the original task's named helper list) is a genuine, well-reasoned recommendation and not a scope-creep error -- should BACKEND-DEV fix it in the same pass or should it be split out? Use your judgement, but note the design's own reasoning for including it (same file, same bug, same caller) is sound if you don't find a reason to disagree; (7) confirm the design contains no implementation code (prose/pseudocode signatures are fine per Type E, but no full function bodies) and correctly scopes to quota_enforcement.zig only; (8) run lint_design_artefact.py and require exit 0 with no BLOCKER/MAJOR.

result.summary: Validated src/design/iss0622-quota-usage-table-schema-qualification.md against current source (not the design doc's paraphrasing). schemaNameForTenant (src/db/pool.zig:137-155) confirmed: copies 'tenant_' prefix then every tenant_id byte except '-', no identifier quoting -- the design's SS3.3 injection-safety claim holds given tenant_id is a canonical UUID (charset [0-9a-f-] contains no SQL metacharacters); this rests on the same trust boundary pool.zig itself already relies on, correctly stated as such rather than assumed. resolveAndCacheStorageMode (pool.zig:183-234) and applyRequestStorageRouting (pool.zig:258-301) confirmed: .LEGACY_RLS branch (277-283) issues 'SET search_path TO public' only, no tenant_default reference at the routing layer; StorageMode enum (src/api/tenant_context.zig:18-21) has exactly two variants (LEGACY_RLS, SCHEMA) -- design's SS4 conclusion that tenant_default is the only applicable schema name for .LEGACY_RLS tenants' PER_TENANT-only tables is independently verified, not merely asserted. hasStorageMode/getStorageMode/setStorageMode all confirmed to exist exactly as described in src/api/tenant_context.zig (design correctly hedges on the exact import path/alias rather than guessing wrong; pool.zig's own @import("tenant_context") confirms it is a module alias, consistent with how quota_enforcement.zig already imports pool via @import("pool")). quota_enforcement.zig read in full (336 lines): readUsageForDimension (143), countRows (175), countRowsWhereRecent (209), sumColumn (237), maxColumn (269), tableStorageBytes (302) all match the design's described structure, line numbers, and branch logic exactly, including the repository_artifacts special-case branches in countRows (181-186) and sumColumn's early-return guard (244-246) -- SS5's claim that repository_artifacts branches are already-correct and untouched is confirmed correct. QuotaMiddlewareError taxonomy (38-46) and its main.zig HTTP mapping (main.zig ~528-545) confirmed consistent with SS6a's claim of no new error variants. Design is concrete enough for BACKEND-DEV to implement without re-deriving decisions: exact function signature for resolveTenantSchema is given (SS3.1), exact SQL text and buffer sizing for all three affected call sites is given (SS3.2), and the decision to resolve schema once in readUsageForDimension rather than per-helper is justified with a followable rationale rather than left to the implementer to re-derive. tableStorageBytes scope-expansion recommendation (SS7) judged sound on independent review, not merely deferred to: it is the same file, same caller (readUsageForDimension's .entity_storage branch), same bug (unqualified name fed into pg_total_relation_size($1::regclass), which resolves via search_path the same way an unqualified FROM does), and reuses the identical schema-qualified name SS2 already computes -- no distinct risk surface, no separate testing/review burden that would justify splitting it into its own issue; leaving it unfixed would leave a structurally identical instance of the exact ISS-0622 defect in the same file. No implementation code present -- SS3.1's function signature and SS3.2's SQL text fragments are prose/pseudocode per Type E, no complete function bodies; scope correctly confined to quota_enforcement.zig only (SS7's file list, SS9's git diff --stat verification criterion). tools/lint_design_artefact.py exits 0, BLOCKER=0, MAJOR=0, MINOR=6 (all cosmetic: quoting real SQL identifiers like 'public.tenant' that the design is transcribing verbatim from pool.zig source comments, plus the ISS-0622 ID not matching the <PREFIX>-<NN> requirement-ID format, which is expected for a bugfix design keyed to an issue ID rather than a requirement ID) -- acceptance criterion of 'no BLOCKER/MAJOR' satisfied.
